And that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death; because he hath spoken to turn [you] away from the LORD your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, to thrust thee out of the way which the LORD thy God commanded thee to walk in. q: A Nazirite’s consecrated period is interrupted when someone dies suddenly beside him. Which plan follows the specified restoration rather than merely extending the old count?

Keep the old count after the birds, because only deliberate corpse contact invalidates earlier days.
Finish the old count first, then bring the ordinary completion offerings without the interruption procedure.
Complete the stated cleansing and offerings, reconsecrate the separation, and do not count the former days.
correctAnswer: Complete the stated cleansing and offerings, reconsecrate the separation, and do not count the former days.

scripture.excerpt: All the days that he separateth [himself] unto the LORD he shall come at no dead body. q: A clean Israelite at home treats the later Passover as an elective delay; a sojourner asks whether participation removes the original ordinance’s conditions. Which answer preserves both passages?

Anyone may elect the later date, but a sojourner must invent a separate rite because he is outside the ordinance.
The later provision is for distant travelers only, while sojourners may participate without the conditions in Exodus.

correctAnswer: Keep the later provision conditional, hold the clean nontraveler accountable, and retain the sojourner’s ordinance requirements.

q: An official applies the lost-property return rule to a servant who has escaped from his master to the community. Which response preserves the explicit distinction?
options: Return him only if his master identifies him, using the unknown-owner property procedure.
Keep him as the finder’s possession, because the property rule allows keeping anything not returned.
Do not return that escaped servant to his master; allow the stated choice of dwelling and do not oppress him.
Return him as lost property, then let him choose his dwelling after his master approves.
correctAnswer: Do not return that escaped servant to his master; allow the stated choice of dwelling and do not oppress him.

scripture.excerpt: ¶ Thou shalt not deliver unto his master the servant which is escaped from his master unto thee: He shall dwell with thee, [even] among you, in that place which he shall choose in one of thy gates, where it liketh him best: thou shalt not oppress him.

supportingScriptures.excerpt: Thou shalt not see thy brother’s ox or his sheep go astray, and hide thyself from them: thou shalt in any case bring them again unto thy brother. And if thy brother [be] not nigh unto thee, or if thou know him not, then thou shalt bring it unto thine own house, and it shall be with thee until thy brother seek after it, and thou shalt restore it to him again. In like manner shalt thou do with his ass; and so shalt thou do with his raiment; and with all lost thing of thy brother’s, which he hath lost, and thou hast found, shalt thou do likewise: thou mayest not hide thyself.

explain: Deuteronomy 23 expressly forbids delivering the described escaped servant to his master and protects dwelling and freedom from oppression. The adjacent-book lost-property duty does not erase that person-specific instruction; the passage does not require inventing his origin.

q: An owner treats every servant as inheritable property and sends a Hebrew servant away empty after six years. Which correction respects the passages without flattening their distinct categories?
options: Treat the six-year release as optional at the owner’s choice by using the foreign-bondservant inheritance provision.
Release the Hebrew servant after six years but omit furnishing, because release alone fulfills Deuteronomy’s requirement.
Apply every foreign-bondservant provision to the impoverished brother, provided the owner avoids harsh treatment.
Retain Hebrew release with provision, voluntary continuation, and Leviticus’ distinction between brothers and foreign bondservants.
correctAnswer: Retain Hebrew release with provision, voluntary continuation, and Leviticus’ distinction between brothers and foreign bondservants.

scripture.excerpt: ¶ [And] if thy brother, an Hebrew man, or an Hebrew woman, be sold unto thee, and serve thee six years; then in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free from thee. And when thou sendest him out free from thee, thou shalt not let him go away empty: Thou shalt furnish him liberally out of thy flock, and out of thy floor, and out of thy winepress: [of that] wherewith the LORD thy God hath blessed thee thou shalt give unto him. And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt, and the LORD thy God redeemed thee: therefore I command thee this thing to day. And it shall be, if he say unto thee, I will not go away from thee; because he loveth thee and thine house, because he is well with thee; Then thou shalt take an aul, and thrust [it] through his ear unto the door, and he shall be thy servant for ever. And also unto thy maidservant thou shalt do likewise. It shall not seem hard unto thee, when thou sendest him away free from thee; for he hath been worth a double hired servant [to thee], in serving thee six years: and the LORD thy God shall bless thee in all that thou doest.

supportingScriptures.excerpt: If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing. If he came in by himself, he shall go out by himself: if he were married, then his wife shall go out with him. If his master have given him a wife, and she have born him sons or daughters; the wife and her children shall be her master’s, and he shall go out by himself. And if the servant shall plainly say, I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free: Then his master shall bring him unto the judges; he shall also bring him to the door, or unto the door post; and his master shall bore his ear through with an aul; and he shall serve him for ever.

¶ And if thy brother [that dwelleth] by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant: [But] as an hired servant, [and] as a sojourner, he shall be with thee, [and] shall serve thee unto the year of jubile: And [then] shall he depart from thee, [both] he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family, and unto the possession of his fathers shall he return. For they [are] my servants, which I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen. Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour; but shalt fear thy God. Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, [shall be] of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids. Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that [are] with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession. And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit [them for] a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever: but over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.

explain: Deuteronomy commands Hebrew release with generous provision and describes voluntary continued service; Exodus also specifies that continued-service choice. Leviticus distinguishes the impoverished brother from inheritable foreign bondservants. The question does not force every term limit into one unstated chronology or modern application.

q: A steward combines the firstfruits presentation and third-year tithe declaration into one priest-only delivery. Which comparison preserves the named recipients and actions?
options: Distinguish firstfruits presentation from third-year sharing within the gates with the four named groups.
Deliver both to the priest alone, because all hallowed produce has identical recipients and location.
Keep the firstfruits at home and take the third-year share only to the altar, reversing the stated settings.
Give both solely to the Levite, because the priest’s firstfruits entitlement ends when the third year arrives.
correctAnswer: Distinguish firstfruits presentation from third-year sharing within the gates with the four named groups.

scripture.excerpt: And it shall be, when thou [art] come in unto the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee [for] an inheritance, and possessest it, and dwellest therein; That thou shalt take of the first of all the fruit of the earth, which thou shalt bring of thy land that the LORD thy God giveth thee, and shalt put [it] in a basket, and shalt go unto the place which the LORD thy God shall choose to place his name there. And thou shalt go unto the priest that shall be in those days, and say unto him, I profess this day unto the LORD thy God, that I am come unto the country which the LORD sware unto our fathers for to give us. And the priest shall take the basket out of thine hand, and set it down before the altar of the LORD thy God. And thou shalt speak and say before the LORD thy God, A Syrian ready to perish [was] my father, and he went down into Egypt, and sojourned there with a few, and became there a nation, great, mighty, and populous: And the Egyptians evil entreated us, and afflicted us, and laid upon us hard bondage: And when we cried unto the LORD God of our fathers, the LORD heard our voice, and looked on our affliction, and our labour, and our oppression: And the LORD brought us forth out of Egypt with a mighty hand, and with an outstretched arm, and with great terribleness, and with signs, and with wonders: And he hath brought us into this place, and hath given us this land, [even] a land that floweth with milk and honey. And now, behold, I have brought the firstfruits of the land, which thou, O LORD, hast given me. And thou shalt set it before the LORD thy God, and worship before the LORD thy God: And thou shalt rejoice in every good [thing] which the LORD thy God hath given unto thee, and unto thine house, thou, and the Levite, and the stranger that [is] among you.

supportingScriptures.excerpt: ¶ When thou hast made an end of tithing all the tithes of thine increase the third year, [which is] the year of tithing, and hast given [it] unto the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow, that they may eat within thy gates, and be filled; Then thou shalt say before the LORD thy God, I have brought away the hallowed things out of [mine] house, and also have given them unto the Levite, and unto the stranger, to the fatherless, and to the widow, according to all thy commandments which thou hast commanded me: I have not transgressed thy commandments, neither have I forgotten [them:]

All the best of the oil, and all the best of the wine, and of the wheat, the firstfruits of them which they shall offer unto the LORD, them have I given thee. [And] whatsoever is first ripe in the land, which they shall bring unto the LORD, shall be thine; every one that is clean in thine house shall eat [of] it.

explain: Deuteronomy describes the firstfruits basket at the chosen place with a confession, then a distinct third-year distribution within the gates. Numbers identifies priestly firstfruits entitlement; it does not erase the other distribution’s named beneficiaries.

q: A man dedicates a field he bought, not his inherited possession, and claims the inherited-field rule makes it the priest’s permanent possession at Jubilee. Which distinction corrects him?
options: Give the field to the buyer’s tribe at Jubilee, because purchase transfers the original family’s permanent possession.
Keep the purchased-field rule distinct: its valuation runs to Jubilee, when it returns to the person whose possession it was.
Apply the inherited-field outcome to every dedicated field, because dedication cancels the purchased-field distinction.
Let the buyer keep the purchased field at Jubilee after paying the fifth required for redeeming his inherited field.
correctAnswer: Keep the purchased-field rule distinct: its valuation runs to Jubilee, when it returns to the person whose possession it was.

scripture.excerpt: And if a man shall sanctify unto the LORD [some part] of a field of his possession, then thy estimation shall be according to the seed thereof: an homer of barley seed [shall be valued] at fifty shekels of silver. If he sanctify his field from the year of jubile, according to thy estimation it shall stand. But if he sanctify his field after the jubile, then the priest shall reckon unto him the money according to the years that remain, even unto the year of the jubile, and it shall be abated from thy estimation. And if he that sanctified the field will in any wise redeem it, then he shall add the fifth [part] of the money of thy estimation unto it, and it shall be assured to him. And if he will not redeem the field, or if he have sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed any more. But the field, when it goeth out in the jubile, shall be holy unto the LORD, as a field devoted; the possession thereof shall be the priest’s. And if [a man] sanctify unto the LORD a field which he hath bought, which [is] not of the fields of his possession; Then the priest shall reckon unto him the worth of thy estimation, [even] unto the year of the jubile: and he shall give thine estimation in that day, [as] a holy thing unto the LORD. In the year of the jubile the field shall return unto him of whom it was bought, [even] to him to whom the possession of the land [did belong].

supportingScriptures.excerpt: ¶ The land shall not be sold for ever: for the land [is] mine; for ye [are] strangers and sojourners with me. And in all the land of your possession ye shall grant a redemption for the land. ¶ If thy brother be waxen poor, and hath sold away [some] of his possession, and if any of his kin come to redeem it, then shall he redeem that which his brother sold. And if the man have none to redeem it, and himself be able to redeem it; Then let him count the years of the sale thereof, and restore the overplus unto the man to whom he sold it; that he may return unto his possession. But if he be not able to restore [it] to him, then that which is sold shall remain in the hand of him that hath bought it until the year of jubile: and in the jubile it shall go out, and he shall return unto his possession.

explain: Leviticus 27 expressly distinguishes a purchased field from a field of one’s possession and directs its Jubilee return to the original possessor. The inherited-field provisions and ordinary land-redemption context cannot erase that specific distinction.

q: A reader says Yeshua’s Sabbath reply rests on the claim that sanctuary work and priestly bread have no Torah restrictions. Which comparison best respects his actual appeal?
options: He accepts that all priestly Sabbath service is blameworthy, then asks that the disciples receive the same punishment.
He removes the bread’s priestly recipients from the Torah and describes the Sabbath offerings as a later custom.
He invokes restricted bread and blameless Sabbath service, rather than claiming the Torah has no such instructions.
He says the bread was unrestricted household food and that the Sabbath offerings were an unlawful priestly invention.
correctAnswer: He invokes restricted bread and blameless Sabbath service, rather than claiming the Torah has no such instructions.

scripture.excerpt: At that time Jesus went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungred, and began to pluck the ears of corn, and to eat. But when the Pharisees saw [it], they said unto him, Behold, thy disciples do that which is not lawful to do upon the sabbath day. But he said unto them, Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him; How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests? Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless? But I say unto you, That in this place is [one] greater than the temple. But if ye had known what [this] meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless. For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.

supportingScriptures.excerpt: ¶ And thou shalt take fine flour, and bake twelve cakes thereof: two tenth deals shall be in one cake. And thou shalt set them in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the LORD. And thou shalt put pure frankincense upon [each] row, that it may be on the bread for a memorial, [even] an offering made by fire unto the LORD. Every sabbath he shall set it in order before the LORD continually, [being taken] from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant. And it shall be Aaron’s and his sons’; and they shall eat it in the holy place: for it [is] most holy unto him of the offerings of the LORD made by fire by a perpetual statute.

¶ And on the sabbath day two lambs of the first year without spot, and two tenth deals of flour [for] a meat offering, mingled with oil, and the drink offering thereof: [This is] the burnt offering of every sabbath, beside the continual burnt offering, and his drink offering.

explain: Matthew expressly calls the bread restricted and the priests’ Sabbath service blameless. Leviticus assigns the bread to Aaron’s family, and Numbers commands Sabbath offerings. This tests the examples Yeshua invokes, without making an unstated ruling about every Sabbath case.

q: A teacher uses Paul’s refusal to charge his hearers to claim that appointed material support was never a real right. Which reading preserves both Torah provision and Paul’s argument?
options: Paul’s nonuse proves the Torah portions were voluntary gifts with no assigned recipients.
The Torah portions require Paul to charge every hearer, so his stated nonuse must mean he took payment privately.
Paul rejects any connection between altar service and support, making the Torah passages irrelevant to his comparison.
Preserve assigned altar portions, Paul’s support analogy and his voluntary nonuse of the right he states.
correctAnswer: Preserve assigned altar portions, Paul’s support analogy and his voluntary nonuse of the right he states.

scripture.excerpt: And the priest shall burn the fat upon the altar: but the breast shall be Aaron’s and his sons’. And the right shoulder shall ye give unto the priest [for] an heave offering of the sacrifices of your peace offerings. He among the sons of Aaron, that offereth the blood of the peace offerings, and the fat, shall have the right shoulder for [his] part. For the wave breast and the heave shoulder have I taken of the children of Israel from off the sacrifices of their peace offerings, and have given them unto Aaron the priest and unto his sons by a statute for ever from among the children of Israel.

supportingScriptures.excerpt: ¶ And the LORD spake unto Aaron, Behold, I also have given thee the charge of mine heave offerings of all the hallowed things of the children of Israel; unto thee have I given them by reason of the anointing, and to thy sons, by an ordinance for ever. This shall be thine of the most holy things, [reserved] from the fire: every oblation of theirs, every meat offering of theirs, and every sin offering of theirs, and every trespass offering of theirs, which they shall render unto me, [shall be] most holy for thee and for thy sons. In the most holy [place] shalt thou eat it; every male shall eat it: it shall be holy unto thee. And this [is] thine; the heave offering of their gift, with all the wave offerings of the children of Israel: I have given them unto thee, and to thy sons and to thy daughters with thee, by a statute for ever: every one that is clean in thy house shall eat of it.

Do ye not know that they which minister about holy things live [of the things] of the temple? and they which wait at the altar are partakers with the altar? Even so hath the Lord ordained that they which preach the gospel should live of the gospel. But I have used none of these things: neither have I written these things, that it should be so done unto me: for [it were] better for me to die, than that any man should make my glorying void. For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of: for necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel! For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward: but if against my will, a dispensation [of the gospel] is committed unto me. What is my reward then? [Verily] that, when I preach the gospel, I may make the gospel of Christ without charge, that I abuse not my power in the gospel.

explain: The Torah specifies priestly portions. Paul refers to those ministering about holy things and states gospel support, then explains his own nonuse. A voluntary waiver is not a denial that the stated provision exists.

q: A commentator says Aaron’s burned goat in Leviticus 10 simply followed the sanctuary-blood exception, and uses Hebrews to make every sin offering inedible. Which assessment preserves the evidence and its limits?
options: That goat lacked inner blood; Moses accepts Aaron’s different explanation, without changing the sanctuary-blood rule or expanding Hebrews’ comparison.
The goat’s blood stayed outside, and Moses accepts Aaron’s explanation; that acceptance establishes a general permission to burn any sin offering during bereavement.
The goat’s blood stayed outside, but the congregation’s sin offering is burned in every case; Hebrews confirms that recipient-based exception.
Moses is content because Aaron invokes the annual atonement disposal rule; Hebrews extends that annual rule to offerings whose blood remains outside.
correctAnswer: That goat lacked inner blood; Moses accepts Aaron’s different explanation, without changing the sanctuary-blood rule or expanding Hebrews’ comparison.

scripture.excerpt: ¶ And Moses diligently sought the goat of the sin offering, and, behold, it was burnt: and he was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron [which were] left [alive], saying, Wherefore have ye not eaten the sin offering in the holy place, seeing it [is] most holy, and [God] hath given it you to bear the iniquity of the congregation, to make atonement for them before the LORD? Behold, the blood of it was not brought in within the holy [place:] ye should indeed have eaten it in the holy [place], as I commanded. And Aaron said unto Moses, Behold, this day have they offered their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD; and such things have befallen me: and [if] I had eaten the sin offering to day, should it have been accepted in the sight of the LORD? And when Moses heard [that], he was content.

supportingScriptures.excerpt: Speak unto Aaron and to his sons, saying, This [is] the law of the sin offering: In the place where the burnt offering is killed shall the sin offering be killed before the LORD: it [is] most holy. The priest that offereth it for sin shall eat it: in the holy place shall it be eaten, in the court of the tabernacle of the congregation. Whatsoever shall touch the flesh thereof shall be holy: and when there is sprinkled of the blood thereof upon any garment, thou shalt wash that whereon it was sprinkled in the holy place. But the earthen vessel wherein it is sodden shall be broken: and if it be sodden in a brasen pot, it shall be both scoured, and rinsed in water. All the males among the priests shall eat thereof: it [is] most holy. And no sin offering, whereof [any] of the blood is brought into the tabernacle of the congregation to reconcile [withal] in the holy [place], shall be eaten: it shall be burnt in the fire.

And the bullock [for] the sin offering, and the goat [for] the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy [place], shall [one] carry forth without the camp; and they shall burn in the fire their skins, and their flesh, and their dung.

For the bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin, are burned without the camp. Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate. Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach.

explain: Leviticus 10 expressly denies inner blood for that goat and records Aaron’s appeal to that day’s calamities, after which Moses is content. Leviticus 6 and 16 govern sanctuary-blood offerings; Hebrews invokes that specific outside-burning pattern. The narrative does not state a universal new exemption for every bereavement.

q: A strong ruler claims that public leadership, a personal revelation and success authorize him to overrule priests and burn sanctuary incense. Which assessment follows all four passages without collapsing their offices?
options: Retain priestly incense duties and test prophetic claims, but treat Joshua’s Spirit-endowed charge as removing his need for Eleazar’s inquiry.
Keep Eleazar’s role, royal submission to law and prophetic tests distinct; Uzziah’s royal strength does not authorize incense ministry.
Retain Eleazar’s role and priestly incense duties, but treat writing the king’s law copy as completing the duty without continued reading.
Retain royal law-reading and distinguish priestly incense, but accept speech in another god’s name if the predicted event occurs.
correctAnswer: Keep Eleazar’s role, royal submission to law and prophetic tests distinct; Uzziah’s royal strength does not authorize incense ministry.

scripture.excerpt: ¶ And the LORD said unto Moses, Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom [is] the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him; And set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation; and give him a charge in their sight. And thou shalt put [some] of thine honour upon him, that all the congregation of the children of Israel may be obedient. And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall ask [counsel] for him after the judgment of Urim before the LORD: at his word shall they go out, and at his word they shall come in, [both] he, and all the children of Israel with him, even all the congregation. And Moses did as the LORD commanded him: and he took Joshua, and set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation: And he laid his hands upon him, and gave him a charge, as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses.

supportingScriptures.excerpt: And it shall be, when he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, that he shall write him a copy of this law in a book out of [that which is] before the priests the Levites: And it shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life: that he may learn to fear the LORD his God, to keep all the words of this law and these statutes, to do them: That his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, and that he turn not aside from the commandment, [to] the right hand, or [to] the left: to the end that he may prolong [his] days in his kingdom, he, and his children, in the midst of Israel.

I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee, and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him. And it shall come to pass, [that] whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require [it] of him. But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die. And if thou say in thine heart, How shall we know the word which the LORD hath not spoken? When a prophet speaketh in the name of the LORD, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that [is] the thing which the LORD hath not spoken, [but] the prophet hath spoken it presumptuously: thou shalt not be afraid of him.

¶ But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to [his] destruction: for he transgressed against the LORD his God, and went into the temple of the LORD to burn incense upon the altar of incense. And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him fourscore priests of the LORD, [that were] valiant men: And they withstood Uzziah the king, and said unto him, [It appertaineth] not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the LORD, but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed; neither [shall it be] for thine honour from the LORD God. Then Uzziah was wroth, and [had] a censer in his hand to burn incense: and while he was wroth with the priests, the leprosy even rose up in his forehead before the priests in the house of the LORD, from beside the incense altar. And Azariah the chief priest, and all the priests, looked upon him, and, behold, he [was] leprous in his forehead, and they thrust him out from thence; yea, himself hasted also to go out, because the LORD had smitten him. And Uzziah the king was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a several house, [being] a leper; for he was cut off from the house of the LORD: and Jotham his son [was] over the king’s house, judging the people of the land.

explain: Numbers distinguishes Joshua’s leadership and Eleazar’s inquiry. Deuteronomy subjects kings and prophetic claims to Yah’s word. Chronicles shows priests opposing Uzziah’s incense intrusion and records judgment. These offices and tests cannot be merged into unlimited authority from success or a private claim.
